name: Seputan
confidence_why: Sellato 1992 and Sellato & Soriente 2015 both give Seputan strong penultimate stress, but the two statements come from one fieldworker's passing ethnographic remarks rather than a phonological description, and Sellato 1992 adds that Aoheng proper stresses the final syllable, so the penultimate rule holds for the Seputan dialect only.

catalog_quote: The Seputan occupied the whole drainage of the Kacu River until they were removed some distance downstream by a government program in the early 1970s. They comprise three autonomous groups: upper Kacu, lower Kacu, and Penané. ... All these people became true swidden farmers by the turn of the twentieth century. Seputan language (some 500 speakers) is closely related to Aoheng, the main difference being its strong stress on the penultimate syllable.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Seputan (one of the two varieties under aohe1237) has strong stress on the penultimate syllable; this is presented as the main feature distinguishing Seputan from the otherwise near-identical Aoheng, which implies Aoheng lacks strong penultimate stress, but the source never says where Aoheng stress falls.

new_statements.domain_note: Impressionistic word-level remark based on Sellato's own field data (all data collected by Sellato, 1970s-80s); no phrase/citation-form distinction made. Applies to the Seputan variety only; Aoheng proper (the variety whose consonant and vowel inventories the article tabulates) receives no stress statement.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement concerns the Seputan variety (upper Kacu / Penane, upper Mahakam), which Glottolog 5.1 subsumes with Aoheng (Penihing) under the language-level code aohe1237 'Aoheng-Seputan' (no separate dialect codes listed). For Aoheng proper the source gives segment inventories but no stress locus; it only implies Aoheng lacks the 'strong' penultimate stress of Seputan. A catalog entry should be labelled 'Seputan variety; Aoheng unstated'.

new_statements.relation_note: For the catalog record as named (Seputan, penultimate: penultimate stress) and the existing Sellato & Soriente 2015 p.344 statement, this 1992 source agrees exactly (Seputan = strong penultimate stress, 'un trait ancien'). It adds the dialect split that the catalog lacks: Aoheng proper is stated to have FINAL-syllable stress. If aohe1237 is treated as the Aoheng language rather than its Seputan dialect, the catalog's penultimate rule would contradict this source for the main variety, so the record should be pinned to sepu1237/Seputan or a second Aoheng = final record added. Same author as the 2015 statement, so this is not an independent observation, but it is the earlier and more explicit…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Seputan: strong word stress on the penultimate syllable (described as a retained old trait). Aoheng proper (the main variety of aohe1237): stress on the final syllable. The same note (p.50) adds that Aoheng villages differ from one another mainly in 'accent' and in the presence or absence of a final glottal stop, without saying what the accent differences are; pp.50-51 otherwise give only segmental remarks (retained /r/ not word-initial, eight phonemic vowels, three genders, transcription conventions).
new_statements.exceptions: none stated; the note is a one-sentence remark, not a phonological description, and gives no examples or conditions
new_statements.identity_note: Sellato 1992 describes the Aoheng (Penihing) of the upper Mahakam, East Kalimantan, and explicitly separates Seputan (three hamlets, 313 people in 1990; Kacü basin, later moved to the Mahakam) from Aoheng proper. The stress remark gives different placements for the two: Seputan penultimate, Aoheng final. The catalog record for aohe1237 is named 'Seputan' and its penultimate rule applies to the Seputan dialect [sepu1237] only; Aoheng [aohe1238] should be recorded as final-stress per this source.

readall_conflicts: No disagreement between sources on Seputan: Sellato 1992 (p.51) and Sellato & Soriente 2015 (p.344) both give strong penultimate stress. The only tension is one of identity, not of data: Sellato 1992 states that Aoheng proper stresses the final syllable, whereas the catalog files a penultimate rule under the glottocode aohe1237, whose Glottolog head variety is Aoheng [aohe1238] with Seputan [sepu1237] as a dialect. Read as a statement about Aoheng-the-language, the catalog's penultimate rule is contradicted by this source; read as a statement about the Seputan dialect (which is how the record is named), it is confirmed. Both statements come from the same author (Sellato), so there is a single observer, not two independent ones.
